question: Reconstruct the event order in anomaly/Robbery/Robbery048_x264.mp4 between 14 and 32 seconds.

correlations.description: All cited windows belong to the same Phase 2D incident anomaly/Robbery/Robbery048_x264.mp4:i0 in the same video.
The interval for f7 occurs before f8-f9, which occur before f10-f12, which occur before f13-f14, which occur before f15.
Compatible RoadAccidents hypotheses persist across adjacent windows f8 to f9.
Compatible Shooting hypotheses persist across adjacent windows f10 to f12.
Compatible RoadAccidents hypotheses persist across adjacent windows f13 to f14.

Person detections from the object source temporally overlap Shooting hypotheses from the surveillance_event source in the same windows; this indicates source co-occurrence only and does not confirm involvement or a crime.

inferences.text: The available evidence suggests the model-produced order between ~14.9s and ~31.9s was: Shooting hypothesis with 3 persons, then RoadAccidents hypothesis with 1 person, then Shooting hypothesis with 1 to 2 to 0 persons, then RoadAccidents hypothesis with 2 to 3 persons.

The evidence indicates an increase from 3 person detections to 9 person detections at ~32s overlapping a continued RoadAccidents hypothesis, which is consistent with a change in scene density but insufficient to determine cause or roles.

limitations: Surveillance_event labels are model hypotheses with modest confidence (RoadAccidents 0.3065-0.5184, Shooting 0.3823-0.4221) and generic_action confidences are low (0.0305-0.2508); they must not be treated as confirmed crimes.
Person detections temporally overlapping an event hypothesis do not mean the detected persons were involved.
Small gaps exist between evidence windows and there is no access to footage, so continuity between windows cannot be verified.
Evidence is insufficient to identify suspects, victims, or causation.

The evidence indicates persistent Shooting hypotheses (0.4221, 0.4181, 0.4087) with cleaning floor at low confidence, while person detections change from 1 to 2 to 0 and a toilet detection appears in the first window.
The evidence indicates persistent RoadAccidents hypotheses (0.4728 then 0.5184) overlapping 2 then 3 person detections and cleaning floor at low confidence.
The evidence indicates 9 person detections (max 0.9125) overlapping a RoadAccidents hypothesis (0.4158) and slapping (0.0305) at the 32s boundary.

findings.text: The retrieved evidence supports the following model-produced order: Shooting hypothesis with 3 persons, then RoadAccidents hypotheses with 1 person, then Shooting hypotheses with 1 to 2 to 0 persons, then RoadAccidents hypotheses with 2 to 3 persons. The surveillance-event model produced these hypotheses; the available evidence is consistent with this sequence but does not establish crimes, involvement, or causality.

The retrieved evidence supports persistent 1-person detections overlapping RoadAccidents hypotheses (0.4406 then 0.3065) and persistent 2- then 3-person detections overlapping RoadAccidents hypotheses (0.4728 then 0.5184). In the 19.2s-21.2s window the evidence indicates suitcase (0.4758), toilet (0.768) and cleaning floor (0.0356) detections; eating chips (0.0427) is indicated only in the earlier 17.067s-19.067s window, not in the later window.

The retrieved evidence supports persistent Shooting hypotheses (0.4221, 0.4181, 0.4087) with cleaning floor at low confidence, while person detections change from 1 to 2 to 0 and a toilet detection (0.7174) appears in the first window of this group.

Person detections from the object source temporally overlap Shooting hypotheses from the surveillance-event source in the same windows. The available evidence indicates source co-occurrence only and does not establish involvement or a crime.

The retrieved evidence supports an increase from 3 person detections to 9 person detections (max 0.9125) at the 32s boundary overlapping a continued RoadAccidents hypothesis (0.5184 then 0.4158) with slapping at low confidence (0.0305). The available evidence is consistent with a change in scene density but is insufficient to determine cause or roles.

report.summary: Between the 14-32 second interval, the retrieved evidence supports alternating Shooting and RoadAccidents model hypotheses with varying person counts and low-confidence generic actions, ending with an increase in person detections at the 32s boundary. All labels are model hypotheses and do not establish crimes, roles, or causality.
